title: Experimental methods and practical skills
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Eduqas A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: MS06-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; MS06-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; MS06-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; MS06-1#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: MS06-1#N.4, MS06-1#N.7, MS06-1#N.12, MS06-1#N.13.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Control variables
items.clue: Everything else that could affect the result, kept fixed.

items.label: Independent variable
items.clue: The one quantity you deliberately change in an experiment.

items.label: Conclusion
items.clue: Statement of what the data show, only within the range tested.

items.label: Systematic error
items.clue: Kind of fault that repeating readings does not cure: change or correct the method instead.

questions.stem: On a pair of vernier callipers, the vernier's zero lies between the 31 mm and 32 mm marks of the main scale. Vernier mark 6 lines up exactly with a main-scale mark. What is the reading?
questions.explanation: Main scale up to the vernier's zero: 31 mm. Vernier mark 6 lines up: 6 × 0.1 mm = 0.6 mm. Reading = 31.6 mm.

questions.stem: One complete cycle of a wave on an oscilloscope screen spans 2.5 divisions. The time-base is set to 2.0 ms div⁻¹. What is the frequency of the signal?
A student investigates how the time t for a ball to fall from rest depends on the drop height h. (h = ½gt², with g constant.) Which plan is best?

options.text: Drop the ball once from each of three heights, timing by hand; plot t against h.
Drop the ball three times from each of six heights, timing electronically; plot h against t.
Drop the ball three times from each of six heights, timing electronically; plot h against t².
Drop a ball three times from each of six heights, timing electronically, with a heavier ball for the greater heights.

questions.explanation: Enough values, repeats, no reaction time, and h = (g/2)t² gives a straight line through the origin with gradient g/2.

questions.stem: A student has a ruler with 1 mm divisions and wants the thickness of one sheet of paper, about 0.1 mm. Which choice and reason are both correct?

options.text: Measure one sheet ten times and average, because averaging reduces the uncertainty.
Measure a stack of 200 sheets and divide by 200, because the reading uncertainty is shared out.
Measure a stack of 10 sheets ten times and average, because more readings always help.
Measure a stack of 200 sheets and divide by 200, because any calibration error in the ruler then cancels.
